question: Why are these powers called Kālikās and how are they presented in the Sāraśāstra?
premises: These powers are known through the cognition of determinate measure.
In some sources they are called Kālikās.
The Sāraśāstra speaks of worshiping the supreme one-syllabled power at the center.
inference: Because they are apprehended as determinate measures of manifestation, these powers are called Kālikās, and the Sāraśāstra centers them in the supreme one-syllabled reality.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal reason for the name Kālikā is only suggested here through iyattākalanā.
plain_english: Because they are known through a determinate measuring, these powers are in some places called Kālikās; and the Sāraśāstra also speaks of the supreme one-syllabled power at the center.
